feature: A sound's waveform is one smooth shape in its lane's colour
summary: A sound's waveform on the timeline is now one smooth filled shape instead of a row of thin bars, and it and the level line over it are drawn in the lane's own colour: cyan on the first sound track, purple on the second. A sound on its own track wears its name in the mock's dark tag. The lane is still 34 points tall; how tall it should be is on a card for you.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walks: Scripts/playtest/fade-diamonds-and-level-points-look-like-the-mock-walk.json and a-sound-s-waveform-follows-its-level-walk.json.

try.do: Open the talk sample from the captions tutorial and look at the Audio lane under V1.
Switch the Mac to light appearance and look again.
Pick the sound and drag the diamond at its top left to about one second.
Drag the level line down a little and let go.
Add the sample music from the Audio menu so it lands on a second sound track, and read its name at its top left.
Compare with the lanes in the audio mock.

evaluate: Does the smooth shape read as the sound better than the bars did?
Is the cyan level line easy enough to find over the cyan waveform, or should it stand out more than the mock draws it?
Does the purple on the second track make it obvious which line belongs to which sound?
Does the music's name in its dark tag read at a glance over the purple waveform?
Having seen it at 34 points, how tall do you want the lane? The card asks.
rough: The mock's sound lane is 84 points tall (72 in a narrow window); ours is still 34, because video.html draws it 28 and the extra 50 points come out of the picture on every recording. Waiting on decision a-sound-lane-is-as-tall-as-the-mock-s-and-its-wa-how-tall-should-a-sound-s-lane-b.

At 34 points the fade diamond still sits on the level line at normal level, which the taller lane would fix. Same decision, a-sound-lane-is-as-tall-as-the-mock-s-and-its-wa-how-tall-should-a-sound-s-lane-b.

The mock's track name sits at the top of a tall lane; ours is centred, which only matters once the lane is taller. Same decision, a-sound-lane-is-as-tall-as-the-mock-s-and-its-wa-how-tall-should-a-sound-s-lane-b.

The audio mock draws the lane in the neutral panel colour with a thin edge in the lane's colour; ours keeps the shared kit's green sound clip from video.html. Covered by a-sound-clip-on-the-timeline-wears-its-file-name.

The sound under V1 still shows no name: the picture right above names it, as decided before this task. A sound on its own track shows its name in the mock's .cliptag, which is how video-audio.html's own lanes are drawn. Matches.
The level line keeps a faint dark shadow the mock does not draw, so it stays visible where it crosses the same-coloured waveform. The app goes further than the mock here.
The icon strip (the timing strip on a picture) keeps its bars and white line; only the video timeline changed.
